mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% for three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% and remains there for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates labor market stress, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, and thus predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in consumer spending (proxied by HOUST) signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening demand, which amplifies recession risk and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and HOUST falls concurrently for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% in a single month, combined with a flat unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates labor market tightness without wage inflation, which historically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 days as firms expand capacity.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS jumps >2% MoM YoY-adjusted while UNRATE is flat
regime_hint: tight labor market without wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during episodes of strong PAYEMS growth with flat UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% for four consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to consider tightening, which reduces corporate earnings growth and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise above 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed their 12-month MAs simultaneously.
